experiment.title: Pendulum at 50°
experiment.headline: g = 9.80 ± 0.10 m/s²
experiment.blurb: A big swing breaks the textbook formula. Then the ghost predicts a second trial.
experiment.description: A steel nut on 62 cm of string, released from about 50 degrees.

scene.description: A heavy nut hangs from a string and swings in a plane parallel to the wall. An A4 sheet is taped to the wall behind it.

tracked_objects.why: The fixed end of the string.

initial_hypotheses.name: Nonlinear pendulum
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The exact pendulum with no losses: gravity pulling the bob back along a circle.
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

initial_hypotheses.name: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The exact pendulum plus drag proportional to speed (air and pivot).
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The amplitude decays exponentially: every swing is the same fraction smaller than the one before. If γ fits to zero, damping is not needed.

initial_hypotheses.name: Small-angle oscillator
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The textbook small-angle pendulum, where the restoring force is proportional to the angle and the period does not depend on the amplitude.
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The period is the same at every amplitude. At 50° a real pendulum is about 7% slower, so the phase drifts out of step within a few swings.

models.name: Nonlinear pendulum
models.mechanism: The exact pendulum with no losses: gravity pulling the bob back along a circle.
models.refuting_signature: The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

models.name: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
models.mechanism: The exact pendulum plus drag proportional to speed (air and pivot).
models.refuting_signature: The amplitude decays exponentially: every swing is the same fraction smaller than the one before. If γ fits to zero, damping is not needed.

models.name: Nonlinear pendulum with quadratic air drag
models.mechanism: The exact pendulum plus quadratic air drag, which bites hardest at the fastest part of the swing.
models.refuting_signature: Big swings lose energy faster than small ones; the decay is not exponential.

models.name: Small-angle oscillator
models.mechanism: The textbook small-angle pendulum, where the restoring force is proportional to the angle and the period does not depend on the amplitude.
models.refuting_signature: The period is the same at every amplitude. At 50° a real pendulum is about 7% slower, so the phase drifts out of step within a few swings.
models.rejection_reason: Held-out RMSE 0.0366 rad against 0.016 rad for Nonlinear pendulum: 2.3× worse, and the intervals do not overlap (0.0285 to 0.0413 rad). g was pinned at its bound of 9 m/s², which means the model is bending a parameter to hide a wrong shape. At this amplitude the small-angle period is wrong by several percent, so the phase of the predicted swing walks away from the real one.

quantities.name: Gravitational acceleration
quantities.note: Scales with the length L_eff measured from the video.

confidence_reasons: The winner is the simplest of three models the data cannot tell apart (P1, P2 and P3 have overlapping held-out intervals), chosen by parsimony.
P1 had the lowest held-out error on 0 of 3 splits, so the evidence for it is weak.
caveats: In 5.5 s of swinging, any damping smaller than about 0.02 /s is invisible. Film a longer clip to measure it.
g is quoted for the video-measured length L_eff; with a tape-measured L the value moves by the tape's uncertainty.
conclusion.narrative_md: The swing is the **exact nonlinear pendulum**, g = 9.80 ± 0.10 m/s². The small-angle formula is **refuted** at this 50° amplitude: its held-out error is 2.3× larger, and it only fits by pushing g down to its bound of 9 m/s². Over only 5.5 s the damping is too small to see, so the data **cannot distinguish** the undamped model from the damped ones.

rounds.summary: The nonlinear model is the right physics for a 50° swing and the small-angle alternative is properly rejected. The claim is honest that damping is unresolved.

issues.claim: The conclusion prefers P1 without damping.
issues.evidence: P2 and P3 have the lower held-out error (0.014 rad against 0.016 rad) but the intervals overlap.
issues.detail: State that the preference is by parsimony and that a longer clip would resolve damping.

rounds.response_md: Caveat added to the conclusion: the preference for P1 is by parsimony, not by evidence.

ghosts.model_name: P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping

revision.diagnosis: The real swing shrinks while the ghost keeps its full amplitude: the ghost leads by more and more late in the run. That is the signature of missing damping.
revision.note: P2 (γ = 0.0091 1/s, fitted on trial 1 only) cuts the maximum error from 29.9 mm to 3.52 mm. Adopted.

events.title: Clip normalized
events.body_md: Read **331 frames** at 60 fps (constant frame rate). Time factor 1, jitter 0.4%. Every frame has a real timestamp.

events.title: Wonder watched the clip
events.body_md: A heavy nut hangs from a string and swings in a plane parallel to the wall. An A4 sheet is taped to the wall behind it.

tracked_objects.why: The fixed end of the string.

events.title: SAM 3.1 tracked 2 objects
events.body_md:
- "steel nut" (moving_body): The swinging bob.
- "black clamp" (pivot): The fixed end of the string.

events.title: Scale and timing calibrated
events.body_md: The A4 sheet gives **1.67 mm per pixel** with 0.40% uncertainty. Plane offset 2 cm; camera moved 0.3 px over the clip.

events.title: Hypothesis P1: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
The exact pendulum with no losses: gravity pulling the bob back along a circle.

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\sin\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

events.title: Hypothesis P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md:
The exact pendulum plus drag proportional to speed (air and pivot).

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\sin\theta-\gamma\,\dot\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The amplitude decays exponentially: every swing is the same fraction smaller than the one before. If γ fits to zero, damping is not needed.

events.title: Hypothesis P0: Small-angle oscillator
events.body_md:
The textbook small-angle pendulum, where the restoring force is proportional to the angle and the period does not depend on the amplitude.

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\,\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The period is the same at every amplitude. At 50° a real pendulum is about 7% slower, so the phase drifts out of step within a few swings.

events.title: Hypothesis P3: Nonlinear pendulum with quadratic air drag
events.body_md:
The exact pendulum plus quadratic air drag, which bites hardest at the fastest part of the swing.

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\sin\theta-\kappa\,|\dot\theta|\,\dot\theta$$

**Refuted if:** Big swings lose energy faster than small ones; the decay is not exponential.

events.title: Prediction made before any fit: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
Before looking at a single fit, I expect **Nonlinear pendulum**. I will count it refuted if this happens: The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

The harness scores every model on the last 35% of the motion, which I never see.

events.title: Fit P1: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.8657** (0.859 to 0.872) rad
- ω₀: **0.00831** (-0.0418 to 0.0584) rad/s
- g: **9.796** (9.75 to 9.84) m/s²

Training RMSE **0.0117 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.016 rad** (0.0143 to 0.0185). Lowest on 0 of 3 splits.

events.title: Fit P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.8745** (0.862 to 0.887) rad
- ω₀: **-0.009404** (-0.0621 to 0.0432) rad/s
- g: **9.792** (9.75 to 9.83) m/s²
- γ (damping): **0.01046** (0 to 0.0222) 1/s

Training RMSE **0.0111 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.0137 rad** (0.0126 to 0.0152). Lowest on 1 of 3 splits.

events.title: Fit P3: Nonlinear pendulum with quadratic air drag
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.8745** (0.862 to 0.887) rad
- ω₀: **-0.008668** (-0.061 to 0.0436) rad/s
- g: **9.792** (9.75 to 9.83) m/s²
- κ (air drag): **0.003714** (0 to 0.00828) 1/rad

Training RMSE **0.0111 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.0137 rad** (0.0126 to 0.0152). Lowest on 2 of 3 splits.

events.title: Fit P0: Small-angle oscillator
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.8678** (0.858 to 0.877) rad
- ω₀: **0.127** (0.0523 to 0.202) rad/s
- g: **9** (9 to 9.05) m/s²

Training RMSE **0.0169 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.0366 rad** (0.0285 to 0.0413). Lowest on 0 of 3 splits.

events.title: Rejected P0: Small-angle oscillator
events.body_md: Held-out RMSE 0.0366 rad against 0.016 rad for Nonlinear pendulum: 2.3× worse, and the intervals do not overlap (0.0285 to 0.0413 rad). g was pinned at its bound of 9 m/s², which means the model is bending a parameter to hide a wrong shape. At this amplitude the small-angle period is wrong by several percent, so the phase of the predicted swing walks away from the real one.

events.title: Winner: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md: Nonlinear pendulum has the lowest held-out error among the models that cannot be told apart (P2, P3 overlap with it). The data can't distinguish them; I report the simplest.

events.title: Reviewer, round 1: accept with caveats
events.body_md:
The nonlinear model is the right physics for a 50° swing and the small-angle alternative is properly rejected. The claim is honest that damping is unresolved.

- **minor:** The conclusion prefers P1 without damping. P2 and P3 have the lower held-out error (0.014 rad against 0.016 rad) but the intervals overlap. *(asks: add caveat)*

issues.claim: The conclusion prefers P1 without damping.
issues.evidence: P2 and P3 have the lower held-out error (0.014 rad against 0.016 rad) but the intervals overlap.
issues.detail: State that the preference is by parsimony and that a longer clip would resolve damping.

events.title: Wonder answers round 1
events.body_md: Caveat added to the conclusion: the preference for P1 is by parsimony, not by evidence.

events.title: Confidence: medium
events.body_md:
- The winner is the simplest of three models the data cannot tell apart (P1, P2 and P3 have overlapping held-out intervals), chosen by parsimony.
- P1 had the lowest held-out error on 0 of 3 splits, so the evidence for it is weak.
- The reviewer accepted with caveats.

events.title: Ghost v1 verdict
events.body_md: The ghost stayed within **6 mm** until 4.88 s, then drifted. Largest error **29.9 mm**.

events.title: Why did it drift? Wonder's diagnosis
events.body_md: The real swing shrinks while the ghost keeps its full amplitude: the ghost leads by more and more late in the run. That is the signature of missing damping.

events.title: Revision tested: P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md: P2 (γ = 0.0091 1/s, fitted on trial 1 only) cuts the maximum error from 29.9 mm to 3.52 mm. Adopted.

events.title: Ghost v2 verdict
events.body_md: The ghost stayed within **6 mm** of the real object for the whole clip, predicting 13 s ahead. Largest error **3.52 mm**.
